headline: Check local ferry and seasonal accommodation availability
reservation: Access to cliff walks and public viewpoints typically does not require an entry permit, but visitors should verify seasonal ferry schedules to the islands. Accommodation in remote areas is limited and requires advance booking through official Shetland tourism or local providers; always check for current site-specific closures.

days.title: Volcanic Cliffs and Atlantic Vistas

stops.name: Eshaness
stops.detail: Visit the Eshaness Lighthouse to view dramatic volcanic cliffs shaped by Atlantic forces and review interpretative panels detailing the area's unique geology and archaeology.

days.driving: Allow time for rural island roads; conditions vary significantly with weather.
days.note: The coastal scenery is highly exposed to Atlantic weather; pace your walk according to wind conditions.

intel.title: Lighthouse Access
intel.text: Parking is available near the Eshaness Lighthouse, which serves as the primary trailhead for cliff walks. The lighthouse is a prominent landmark visible from a distance, aiding navigation.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: Specific mobile signal strength for the Eshaness peninsula is not documented in available evidence. Travelers should download offline maps or carry physical navigation aids before leaving gateway hubs.

intel.title: Supply and Fuel Planning
intel.text: Evidence does not specify fuel stations in the immediate Eshaness vicinity. Ensure your vehicle is fueled in larger settlements like Lerwick or Brae before heading to the remote northwest coast.

intel.title: Geological Exploration
intel.text: Allocate time to read the interpretative panels at the start point to understand the volcanic history before walking. The scenery to the north offers the most dramatic views of cliff erosion.

intel.title: Trail Accessibility
intel.text: The Eshaness area is described as highly accessible from the car park. However, visitors should remain cautious near cliff rims where the Atlantic fury has created steep and unstable drops.

plan.arrival: Arrive via ferry or flight to Lerwick, collect a rental vehicle, and secure supplies before driving north toward the Northmavine peninsula.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for paved island roads, though high winds may affect high-profile RVs; check rental agreements for island-specific restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Eshaness cliffs offer expansive westward views for sunset, though maritime fog can frequently obscure the horizon.
